newsitem.title: USA: SEC sues promoter, stockbrokers for fraud.
newsitem.headline: SEC sues promoter, stockbrokers for fraud.

text.p: The New York regional office of the Securities and Exchange Commission said Friday it sued a stock promoter and seven stock brokers for a scheme in which the brokers were bribed to recommend certain stocks.
The civil suit, filed in federal court in Orlando, Fla., alleges that the promoter netted about $2.6 million from the scheme.

The SEC alleged that from January 1992 through June 1993, Atlantic Capital Corp. of Orlando schemed to sell stock it obtained for preparing and distributing brochures that promoted shares of little known, publicly traded companies.
Certain Atlantic officers and employees allegedly bribed brokers to recommend the securities to their retail customers.
The brochures distributed to at least 100,000 investors never disclosed the bribes or Atlantic's ownership of options or stock in the companies being promoted.

The brokers who received bribes worked for First New England Securities Corp., Corporate Securities Group and Paragon Capital Corp., all in Florida; Kemper Securities in Denver Colo. and Covey & Co. in Salt Lake City, Utah.
